A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same fSGLD research work. All 40 pages of v1 and 48 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables and appendices, support comparison; relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original noisy-label classification, fine-tuning, coupling ablation, sensitivity and Hessian-spectrum results in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 reports original fSGLD results for Bayesian classification, OOD detection, noisy-label optimization and coupling studies. Although Tables 1–2 attribute comparator results to prior work, the fSGLD results are original.

M1.justification: The perturbed-gradient Langevin update, randomized-smoothing objective and Hessian-trace target are retained. The β–σ coupling already existed and was used in v1; v2 integrates it into the algorithm exposition. The new Bayesian experiments apply the same optimizer through a shared evaluation protocol.

E1.justification: v2 adds clean-label CIFAR-10/100 Bayesian classification and predictive-uncertainty evaluation, plus SVHN OOD detection. These substantially expand the tasks and input distributions beyond the retained CIFAR-10N/100N and WebVision noisy-label experiments.

E2.justification: New Bayesian comparisons include Entropy-SGD, bSAM, Entropy-SGLD and Entropy-MCMC, with comparator scores attributed to prior work. Conversely, SGLD is removed from the corresponding noisy-label and fine-tuning tables. The Hessian comparison replaces SAM with SGLD.

E3.justification: New protocols use ResNet-18, averaging over 16 parameter snapshots, NLL and entropy-based OOD scoring with AUROC/AUPR. For retained noisy-label experiments, v1 searches σ over 10^[-3,-2] with η=0.01; v2 searches β over 10^[7,9] with η=0.1. Thus the revised fSGLD scores do not represent identical-setting comparisons.

E4.justification: v2 replaces the across-benchmark coupled-versus-fixed-β ablation with controlled sweeps fixing β=10^8 or σ=10^-3 and examining the implied η. It removes v1's n=1–5 perturbation-count accuracy/cost study and revises the Hessian analysis to compare against SGLD instead of SAM.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly reports three-seed means and standard-deviation bars for the coupling sweeps and three-seed results for Bayesian classification; retained noisy-label tables still use five seeds. The reported Hutchinson trace-estimation probe count changes from 1,000 to 100.

E6.justification: v2 adds Bayesian and OOD results, including fSGLD NLL values of 0.144 and 0.810 on CIFAR-10/100. Retained fSGLD results are replaced under revised settings: ResNet-34 CIFAR-100N accuracy changes from 62.02±0.29 to 61.51±0.65. Hessian estimates also change, while removed comparisons and perturbation-count rows eliminate previous results.

T1.justification: v2 adds an expected Taylor-remainder bound outside a compact set, restricts η from η>0 to 0<η<1, and substantially rewrites the Gibbs-discrepancy and convergence proofs. The reported discrepancy changes from O(β^(-η)) to a dimension-dependent bound with leading fixed-d order O(β^(-η/4)); moment and excess-risk constants also change. The W2 iterate result is retained in Corollary D.16.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden the claimed contribution to Bayesian prediction, reliable uncertainty estimates and OOD detection, and explicitly emphasize memory efficiency. v2 drops v1's claim to be the first to combine SGLD with flatness while retaining the central coupling and convergence claims.

C2.justification: v1 Appendix B.3 argues that additional higher-order control is unnecessary; v2 instead explains and justifies its new remainder-control assumption. v2 also discusses exponential dimension/temperature dependence, stronger assumptions needed for improved W2 rates, and stability across η within (0,1). These materially qualify theoretical applicability and revise the coupling interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds technical information on 16-snapshot prediction, σ=10^-3 for Bayesian experiments, OOD test-set concatenation and learning rate 0.5 for coupling sweeps. It revises the search-space table and omits v1's at-most-1,000-example Hessian subsampling description. Software, hardware and the experimental code link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 introduces substantive positioning against Entropy-MCMC and a new Flat Posterior Sampling discussion covering flat-seeking Bayesian networks and flat posterior-aware model averaging. Additional references contextualize higher-order assumptions and convergence limitations, substantially revising the novelty argument beyond v1's optimizer-focused positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, the algorithm precedes the expanded smoothing explanation, and Section 4 is reorganized around Bayesian and optimization perspectives. Experimental setup moves into Appendix E, while a new appendix roadmap and proof subsections reorganize the theoretical narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds Bayesian/OOD tables, removes the perturbation-count table, restructures retained comparison tables and replaces the sensitivity display with paired coupling plots. Hessian plots are redrawn with different axes and comparator labels. The theoretical schematic moves from v1 Figure 1 to v2 Appendix D Figure 3; typography and table placement also change.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful Bayesian/OOD evidence, more targeted coupling experiments and clearer theoretical assumptions. However, its rewritten central proof has an unresolved inconsistency: Appendix D.1 Eq. (32) defines C1 that approaches log 2 for fixed d as β increases, then claims C1=O(β^(-η)d²). That calculation does not establish the advertised vanishing discrepancy. With this central reliability concern and the loss of direct noisy-label SGLD comparisons, the benefits do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
